d3m1-a1.title: Exhibit Packet Audit — the Demand Package as drafted
d3m1-a1.kicker: Audit the enclosure set before Atty. Thorne signs anything.
d3m1-a1.intro: The demand specialist built the enclosure set and typed the Specials from it. Nothing has been re-verified since the pre-demand audit and no corrected record has been chased. Work the set item by item: every loophole here is one Dana Whitfield can use, and every gap is one she will find.

items.as: Cited as RPD-26-018824; portal download of 02/26/2026.
items.issue: The report is RPD-26-018842. A demand that cites a report number that does not exist invites the adjuster to say our liability proof cannot be located, and the transposition is already in our own intake sheet.
items.fix: Order the certified complete report under the correct number, correct the intake record with a note citing the report, and assign both as dated CMS tasks.

items.as: Scene original, scanned; signed and dated 02/06/2026.
items.issue: An independent witness who signed at the scene is the answer to the comparative-negligence line defense counsel pressed later. The copy is the signed original.
items.fix: Confirm the signature and date are legible on the scan, and that a signed follow-up statement has been requested before memories fade.

items.as: Four stills, grayscale export of the 02/19/2026 working copy.
items.issue: The clearest liability proof on the file, and in grayscale the stop line and the signal are hard to read. An exhibit the adjuster cannot see is an exhibit she can ignore.
items.fix: Re-export the four stills in color from the native file, hash unchanged, and enclose the preservation and chain-of-custody log with them.

items.as: Certified copy, run RF-26-0206-114, from Riverton Fire records.
items.issue: This is the document that answers the fourteen days: a neck complaint recorded at the scene on the date of loss, and "restrained front-seat passenger" against the later unbelted defense.
items.fix: Confirm it is the certified copy and that the demand's section 3 quotes it, not paraphrases it.

items.what: Riverton Spine & Rehab itemized LOP ledger
items.as: 34 lines, $6,290.00, as the provider's portal produced it.
items.issue: 05/04/2026 is billed twice. The attendance log shows 33 attended visits, so the audited figure is 33 × $185.00 = $6,105.00. A demand built on a duplicate is a demand the carrier can discredit line by line.
items.fix: Request the Final Itemized Ledger with the duplicate removed, re-verify the balance with the provider in the week of service, and update the Specials.

items.as: Bills John Doe $1,540.00 as due from the patient.
items.issue: The $1,540.00 is the contractual adjustment. Crescent is in network, was paid $1,860.00 at the contract rate, and cannot balance-bill the member. Enclosing it asserts a balance that does not exist and invites a lien that does not exist.
items.fix: Ask Crescent for a corrected $0.00 patient statement, enclose it with Peach State's EOB, and never list Crescent as an open balance.

items.as: Dr. Helen Park's read; the history line gives the date of injury as 02/16/2026.
items.issue: The date of loss is 02/06/2026. A ten-day error inside our own causation exhibit is exactly what an adjuster uses to argue the herniation came from something else, and it sits on the one document that answers "degenerative".
items.fix: Request a corrected history addendum from Summit Imaging and enclose the report with it; keep Dr. Park's impression quoted word for word in the letter.

items.as: Signed original of 06/19/2026 from Lakeside Orthopedics.
items.issue: The centrepiece: it ties the delayed presentation and the C5-C6 herniation to the collision to a reasonable degree of medical probability, and puts the 2021 low-back care outside the claim.
items.fix: Confirm it is the signed original and that the letter's section 3 cites it by date rather than summarising its opinion in our own words.

items.as: Signed original of 06/30/2026 from Northgate HR.
items.issue: It proves the $1,584.00 twice over: nine missed shifts for the wage claim, and the 02/09–02/13/2026 call-outs that show symptoms before first treatment.
items.fix: Confirm the call-out record is attached to it, so the wage proof and the gap corroboration travel together.

items.what: Margaret Doe's Civic: estimate, supplement and Diminished Value report
items.as: Fourteen pages from the Property Damage sub-file, enclosed with the medical exhibits.
items.issue: It is not even Mr. Doe's claim. The parked Civic is his mother Margaret's, her claim is KM-26-440871-PD with a different adjuster, and putting it inside his bodily injury demand invites a release that reaches her car.
items.fix: Pull it. Keep her claim in its own file, and make sure the demand says in terms that Mr. Doe makes no Property Damage claim and that nothing in it releases hers.

items.as: Four pages of Atty. Thorne's internal summary, enclosed "for context".
items.issue: It names our own gap risk, our own valuation and our internal dates. Sent to the adverse carrier it hands Keystone our weaknesses and our number, and it can never be taken back.
items.fix: Pull it. It never goes in a Demand Package, a Mediation Binder or an arbitration exhibit set; flag to Atty. Thorne that it was in the draft.

items.as: The client's signed authorization, enclosed with the internal summary.
items.issue: An authorization is how the firm gets records from providers. Handing it to the adverse carrier gives Keystone a route to John Doe's medical file that we do not control and did not have to give.
items.fix: Pull it. Keystone receives the records we choose to enclose; calendar the authorization's renewal before it expires on 02/06/2027.

items.what: The exhibit index's own Bates ranges
items.as: Exhibit E runs LSH-DEM-000016–66 and Exhibit F runs LSH-DEM-000064–66.
items.issue: The two ranges overlap, so three pages belong to two exhibits at once. Once the carrier cites a Bates number, nobody can be sure which document was meant — and the index is the one thing both sides rely on.
items.fix: Re-number the set once the pulls and replacements are done, so every page sits in exactly one exhibit and the ranges match the page counts.

items.as: Not in the set. The nineteen-day April disruption has no exhibit at all.
items.issue: The letter explains the fourteen days, then leaves the April break to be discovered. Keystone will call it failure to mitigate, and the answer — the rental ending 03/19, the carpool ending 04/01, evening visits from 04/21 — is nowhere in the enclosures.
items.fix: Add the Gap Explanation Record: every entry with its underlying record, both intervals, and the A-C-T account of the April break with the attendance log behind it.

items.what: Keystone's declarations page and limits letter
items.as: Not in the set, though the letter's opening relies on it.
items.issue: The whole demand rests on $10,000 being the per-person bodily injury limit. The proof is Keystone's own letter of 03/20/2026. Without it the demand asserts the limit instead of showing it.
items.fix: Add the declarations page and the 03/20/2026 cover letter as the last exhibit, and cite it in the letter's opening and in section 5.

items.what: Each deficiency as a dated, assigned CMS task
items.as: The draft asks the Case Manager to tell the specialist what to change.
items.issue: Fixing a draft quietly leaves no record of who found what, and no way to prove the set was audited before it went out. The terms, the amount and the deadline are Atty. Thorne's and are not the Case Manager's to change at all.
items.fix: Log every finding above as a dated, assigned task; route the corrected set and the audit note to Atty. Thorne for signature. Change no term.

d3m1-a1.revealNote: The Demand Package as Atty. Thorne signed and served it on 07/20/2026: the letter with its four faults corrected and the Exhibit Index as served, 81 pages. Every later activity on this file works from this set.
revealPoints: Specials $14,817.40 medical + $1,584.00 wages = $16,401.40, every line tied to a certified bill.
Acceptance runs 30 days from the adjuster's written acknowledgement of receipt, not from the date of the letter.
A Limited Release of Robert Smith and Keystone Mutual only, preserving every UM/UIM claim and the Property Damage claim.
Robert Smith's affidavit of no other insurance added as condition 3.
Exhibits A–J, 81 pages, Bates LSH-DEM-000001–000081, each exhibit mapped to the section it proves.
Receipt acknowledged in writing 07/22/2026, so the acceptance window closes 08/21/2026, docketed with reminders.

d3m2-rel.title: Release Clause Audit — Keystone's draft release
d3m2-rel.kicker: Call every clause before John Doe sees a word of it.
d3m2-rel.intro: Keystone tendered its $10,000 limits on 08/12/2026 and sent its own release form today, with a cover letter holding the check until both UM carriers consent and waive subrogation. Measure every clause against the demand's terms and the claims still open on this file, propose the fix, and leave every decision to Atty. Thorne.

items.what: Keystone's payment condition: each UM carrier's consent and subrogation waiver
items.as: No check issues until Harbor Point's and Cardinal State's written consents and waivers arrive with the executed release and the W-9.
items.issue: A fair condition: a UM carrier that keeps its subrogation right could later pursue Robert Smith. It also matches what John Doe needs before signing, so the two tasks run together.
items.fix: Log it as a payment condition, tie the signing task to both consents (requested 08/13/2026), and send the waivers with the executed release.

items.what: Claimant, insured, policy and date of accident
items.as: John Doe; Robert Smith; policy KMI-PA-7731045; claim KM-26-440871; accident 02/06/2026 at Maple Hollow Road and Birch Avenue.
items.issue: Every identifier matches Keystone's Declaration Page and the tender letter, so the release attaches to the right claim and nothing has to be reissued for a typo.
items.fix: Confirm each number against the Declaration Page and the tender letter before the release is routed.

items.as: Ten thousand and 00/100 dollars ($10,000.00), the sole consideration.
items.issue: The figure is Keystone's full BI limit as tendered on 08/12/2026 and as the demand asked; a release for less would be a different settlement.
items.fix: Confirm the amount against the tender letter; any change is Atty. Thorne's.

items.what: Parties released: Robert Smith and Keystone Mutual
items.as: Robert Smith and Keystone Mutual Insurance, and their agents, employees, heirs, successors and assigns.
items.issue: These are the parties the demand offered to release, and the parties both UM carriers consented to John Doe releasing.
items.fix: Keep the named parties exactly as written; confirm against the demand's Limited Release term.

items.what: Catch-all discharge of every other person and insurer
items.as: “and all other persons, firms, corporations and insurers, whether herein named or not”.
items.issue: Harbor Point and Cardinal State are insurers. Signed as drafted, the release would discharge both UM claims: $30,000 of John Doe's $40,000 stack, gone for a $10,000 check.
items.fix: Propose: Robert Smith and Keystone only, “and no other person, firm, corporation or insurer”. Quote the words exactly in the review to Atty. Thorne.

items.what: Claims released: bodily injury, Property Damage and Loss of Use
items.as: “including all claims for bodily injury, Property Damage and Loss of Use”.
items.issue: The Civic's Property Damage and loss-of-use claim is Margaret Doe's, open with Leah Moran on KM-26-440871-PD. John Doe cannot release it, and Keystone PD would cite the wording against it.
items.fix: Propose: the bodily injury claim only, with the Civic's claim expressly reserved. Route to Atty. Thorne.

items.as: Nothing in the release preserves John Doe's claims against Harbor Point or Cardinal State.
items.issue: Even with the catch-all struck, a silent release invites Harbor Point or Cardinal State to argue the UM claims were compromised. The protection should sit on the face of the document.
items.fix: Propose a clause reserving the UM/UIM claims by carrier, policy and claim number: HP-26-7741 and CS-26-20355. Atty. Thorne approves the wording.

items.as: The payment compromises a disputed claim and is not an admission of liability by the released parties.
items.issue: Standard: Keystone pays to end the claim, not to admit fault. It costs John Doe nothing and is in every release of this kind.
items.fix: Keep as drafted.

items.as: Injuries may be permanent and progressive; the releasor relies on his own judgment of their nature and extent.
items.issue: Dr. Reyes noted possible repeat injections ($3,400–$6,800). Whether this clause stands, and how it is explained to John Doe, is legal advice.
items.fix: Flag it for Atty. Thorne with the future-care note attached; he decides and goes through it with John Doe before signing.

items.what: Confidentiality of the settlement and the release
items.as: Terms, amount and the release itself not to be disclosed to any person, firm or insurer, with narrow exceptions.
items.issue: Confidentiality was never a term of the demand, and the UM carriers need the signed release as proof of exhaustion. Signed, it would put the UM demands of 08/31/2026 in breach.
items.fix: Propose striking the clause; route to Atty. Thorne with the demand's terms beside it.

items.what: Liens: indemnify, defend and hold harmless
items.as: Releasor warrants every lien is paid and will indemnify, defend and hold harmless, including attorney's fees and costs.
items.issue: An open-ended duty to defend and pay fees on any lien, unlimited in amount, when the file's liens are known: Peach State and Riverton Spine & Rehab.
items.fix: Propose: the liens on the file paid from the firm's trust account; hold harmless limited to the settlement proceeds; no duty to defend, no fees. Atty. Thorne decides.

items.as: Releasor is not and has never been a Medicare beneficiary; no conditional payments.
items.issue: John Doe signs it as a statement of fact. The facts must come from the file, not from assumption: born 08/14/1991, employed at Northgate, no Medicare.
items.fix: Verify the facts from the intake and the Day 2 check, attach them, and flag the clause for Atty. Thorne's approval.

items.as: The release says nothing about when Keystone must pay after it is signed.
items.issue: Without a date the check can drift while John Doe's release is already signed, and the UM demands wait on proof of payment.
items.fix: Propose a payment term for Atty. Thorne to set; docket it once Keystone agrees.

items.as: Governed by “the laws of the state in which it is signed”.
items.issue: Which law governs a release is a legal question, and a vague choice-of-law line can matter if the release is ever disputed.
items.fix: Flag for Atty. Thorne; record his decision on the redline.

items.as: John Doe, Releasor; witness; notary jurat; approved as to form by Atty. Thorne.
items.issue: Keystone requires a notarized wet-ink original, and the block provides for it. Nothing is signed until the amended release and both consents are in.
items.fix: Keep. Plan the signing: notary, photo ID in the name John Doe, Atty. Thorne's review first.

d3m2-rel.revealNote: The release as Atty. Thorne approved it on 08/17/2026 and Keystone reissued it on 08/19/2026, ready for John Doe's signature. Every later step on this file works from it, and the executed copy follows.
revealPoints: Robert Smith and Keystone only, “and no other person, firm, corporation or insurer”: the UM claims are safe.
The bodily injury claim only; HP-26-7741, CS-26-20355 and the Civic's claim KM-26-440871-PD reserved.
Confidentiality struck; the lien clause limited to the liens on the file, paid from trust, no defense or fees.
Payment within 14 days of Keystone's receipt of the executed release and the W-9.
Unknown injuries kept, Medicare kept as verified, State of Riverton law: Atty. Thorne's decisions.

d3m4-pal.title: Lien Investigation — Vance & Kettering's charging lien
d3m4-pal.kicker: Test every claim in the notice against the file; leave every conclusion to Atty. Thorne.
d3m4-pal.intro: Six days before disbursement an outside firm claims a charging lien and $6,666.67 of the fee, on an agreement dated 07/27/2026. Work its notice, agreement and time record item by item against the file, decide what goes into the evidentiary packet for Atty. Thorne, and what is his alone to decide.

items.as: Emailed to Atty. Thorne and the case manager; received 10/14/2026.
items.issue: The notice itself is the trigger: its receipt date starts the file's response and sets what is held before the 10/22/2026 disbursement.
items.fix: Log it on receipt in the Communications Log, route it to Atty. Thorne the same day, and send nothing to the firm.

items.as: 33⅓% of any gross recovery; binding when signed by the client or the client's representative.
items.issue: The firm's own document is the core exhibit: it shows exactly who signed, when, and with what authority attached.
items.fix: Keep the complete copy as received, every page, in the packet and the CMS.

items.what: Who the client is said to be
items.as: “John Doe (by Margaret Doe, mother)”.
items.issue: John Doe is an adult, born 08/14/1991. The agreement attaches no power of attorney or other authority for his mother to act for him; the framing assumes what it must prove.
items.fix: State the facts in the packet instead: adult client, signer Margaret Doe, no authority attached. No conclusion.

items.as: Margaret Doe signed as “mother”; the line for John Doe is blank.
items.issue: The blank client line is the single most important fact in the dispute, and the copy shows it plainly.
items.fix: Keep it, and put it beside John Doe's own signatures for comparison.

items.as: The notice offers nothing to compare the agreement against.
items.issue: Without exemplars the packet asserts rather than shows. John Doe signed the firm's fee agreement and HIPAA authorization on 02/09/2026.
items.fix: Add both 02/09/2026 documents to a signature comparison table in the packet.

items.as: The notice gives only its own date of retention, 07/27/2026.
items.issue: LSH Law Group was engaged 02/09/2026 and served the demand 07/20/2026, before the agreement existed, with no discharge or substitution anywhere on the file.
items.fix: Add a dated timeline cross-referencing the agreement against the firm's engagement milestones, each line sourced.

items.as: The firm says it performed substantial services and helped obtain the $40,000.00.
items.issue: Its own time record shows 0.6 hours: an intake with Margaret Doe and a welcome letter to her. Nothing on the claim, and no document on the file is theirs.
items.fix: Replace the claim in the packet with the work-product audit: the time record's entries quoted, against the file's own work.

items.as: Asserted in the notice, with no letter or date given.
items.issue: Every carrier letter on the file is addressed to LSH Law Group; Keystone, Harbor Point and Cardinal State show no notice from Vance & Kettering.
items.fix: Replace with what the carrier correspondence shows, each letter cited by date.

items.as: 0.4 hours on 07/27/2026 and 0.2 hours on 07/29/2026, both with Margaret Doe; no other entries.
items.issue: The firm's own record of what it did. It is the best evidence of the work actually done, in its own words.
items.fix: Keep it whole in the packet; quote it, never characterize it.

items.as: The notice speaks for the client without his word.
items.issue: Only John Doe can say whether he ever retained the firm. Without his account the packet rests on documents alone.
items.fix: On Atty. Thorne's instruction, ask him neutrally on a recorded call, log his words, and give no view on the lien.

items.what: The settlement hold and the Action Plan
items.as: The notice asks the firm to hold the entire settlement.
items.issue: The 10/22/2026 disbursement depends on this dispute. A hold no one recorded is a hold no one releases.
items.fix: Place the hold Atty. Thorne directs, $6,666.67, in the CMS Trust Ledger; update the Action Plan; record who may release it.

items.as: Half of the one-third fee on a $40,000.00 gross.
items.issue: Whether any fee is owed, and how much, is a legal determination between lawyers.
items.fix: Flag for Atty. Thorne. The Case Manager never discusses, accepts or counters a fee division.

items.what: The charging lien and any quantum meruit claim
items.as: A charging lien against the settlement proceeds.
items.issue: Validity, and whether quantum meruit applies at all where no engagement may exist, are Atty. Thorne's calls.
items.fix: List them in the packet as questions for Atty. Thorne, beside the facts that bear on them.

items.what: “Your case manager” to confirm the fee division by 10/16
items.as: The notice asks the case manager to confirm the split in writing.
items.issue: Any reply from the Case Manager, even a refusal, is the firm speaking on a fee dispute, and could be quoted back.
items.fix: No reply. Flag the request to Atty. Thorne; he answers the lawyer.

d3m4-pal.revealNote: The evidentiary packet as delivered to Atty. Thorne on 10/15/2026: facts only, each sourced. He repudiated the lien on 10/16; Vance & Kettering withdrew it on 10/19/2026, and he released the hold.
revealPoints: The agreement of 07/27/2026 is signed only by Margaret Doe; John Doe's line is blank and no authority is attached.
LSH Law Group was engaged 02/09/2026 and served the demand 07/20/2026, before that agreement.
The firm's time record shows 0.6 hours with Margaret Doe; no carrier received notice from it.
John Doe's account of 10/15: he never contacted or signed with the firm.
$6,666.67 held in trust on Atty. Thorne's instruction; validity and any response left to him.

d3m1-a1.title: Service Confirmation — the email the adjuster has to answer
d3m1-a1.kicker: Sending proves it left. Her written acknowledgement proves when it landed.
d3m1-a1.subject: Time-Limited Demand served today — John Doe / Robert Smith — Claim KM-26-440871
d3m1-a1.brief: Write the email that serves the demand on the adjuster. Say it is served by this email, list what is attached, say the clock runs from her written acknowledgement of receipt, and ask her to confirm the receipt date and a complete set. Terms go to Atty. Thorne.

required.label: Says the demand is served on her by this email
required.hint: Say in terms that the signed demand is served on her with this email.

required.label: Says what is attached: the Demand Package, 81 pages, Exhibits A–J
required.hint: Name the package, the page count and the exhibit range, so she cannot say part was missing.

required.label: States that the 30 days run from her written acknowledgement of receipt
required.hint: The window runs from her written acknowledgement of receipt, not the letter date or send date. Say so.

required.label: Asks her to confirm the receipt date and that the set is complete
required.hint: Ask her to confirm in writing the date she received the email and that the package is complete.

required.label: Routes terms, amount and any extension to Atty. Thorne
required.hint: Point every question about the terms or the deadline to Atty. Thorne, by name.

reply.subject: RE: Time-Limited Demand served today — John Doe / Robert Smith — Claim KM-26-440871
reply.body:
Confirming receipt. Your email of July 20 with the demand and its attachment is in the file, received and opened this morning, July 22; the PDF opens at 81 pages and the index runs A through J, so I show it complete.

I have logged the demand as received 07/22/2026 and diaried it for evaluation. I will need to review the imaging and the treatment records before I can respond to the number. I may come back to you about the time frame.

press.subject: RE: Time-Limited Demand — extension request
press.body: One more thing. Our medical review is backed up and I will not have an evaluation inside thirty days. Can we agree to two more weeks on the acceptance date? If you can just confirm by reply I will note the file at September 4 and we can skip the paperwork.

choices.label: Reply that two weeks is fine and note it on the file.
choices.why: The Case Manager has just moved a deadline Atty. Thorne set. It is his term to change, and a reply like this can be held against the demand later.

choices.label: Reply that the demand stands as written and any request must go in writing to Atty. Thorne; forward it the same day.
choices.why: Correct. Nothing is granted and nothing is refused: the request is recorded, routed the same day, and the 08/21/2026 date stays on the docket until he says otherwise.

choices.label: Say nothing and let the deadline run.
choices.why: An unanswered request is still a request on the file. If Keystone later says it asked and got no response, silence is the record we are left with.

choices.label: Reply that no extensions are granted on a Time-Limited Demand.
choices.why: That is a decision on the terms, and a refusal is as much the attorney's call as an agreement. The Case Manager does not answer it either way.

d3m2-rel.title: Release Review — the clause audit routed to Atty. Thorne
d3m2-rel.kicker: You propose the amendments. Atty. Thorne approves them, in writing, before anyone signs.
d3m2-rel.subject: For your review and approval: Keystone draft release — John Doe — KM-26-440871
d3m2-rel.brief: Write the email that routes your clause review to Atty. Thorne. Say what the catch-all would release, what else the draft reaches or adds, list your proposed amendments, flag the clauses that are his to decide, and confirm nothing has gone to John Doe.

required.label: Names the catch-all and the UM claims it would release
required.hint: Quote the insurers line and say it would release Harbor Point and Cardinal State.

required.label: Says the release reaches the Civic's open Property Damage claim
required.hint: The draft releases Property Damage and Loss of Use: the Civic's claim is Margaret's and still open.

required.label: Raises the confidentiality clause
required.hint: Confidentiality was never a demand term, and the UM carriers need the release.

required.label: Proposes the amendments for his approval
required.hint: Say what you propose for each clause, and that the decision is his.

required.label: Flags the clauses that are his to decide
required.hint: Unknown injuries, Medicare and governing law: name them as his call.

required.label: Confirms nothing has gone to John Doe for signature
required.hint: Say the draft has not been sent to the client and won't be until he approves.
match: not (been )?sent|haven't sent|have not sent|not gone|nothing (has )?(gone|been sent)|withheld|will not send|won't send|not (be )?(sent|shown)

reply.subject: RE: For your review and approval: Keystone draft release — John Doe — KM-26-440871
reply.body:
Approved as you proposed. Payment within 14 days of Keystone's receipt of the executed release and our W-9. Keep the unknown-injuries clause; I will go through it with John. Keep the Medicare representation as verified. Riverton law.

I have sent the redline to Dana Whitfield this morning. Do not send anything to John until Keystone issues the revised release and both consents are in.

press.subject: RE: Doe release — side letter?
press.body: Mr. Thorne's redline is with my unit manager and could take a while. To keep things moving, could your client sign our standard form now? We can paper the changes in a side letter afterwards, and I could get the check out next week.

choices.label: Send John Doe the standard form now so the check is not delayed.
choices.why: John Doe would sign a release that discharges both UM carriers. A side letter promised later protects nothing he has already signed.

choices.label: Agree to the side letter if she confirms it by email.
choices.why: That is agreeing release terms with the adjuster, which is Atty. Thorne's alone, and on terms he has just rejected.

choices.label: Reply that nothing goes to the client except the release Atty. Thorne approves, and forward her email to him the same day.
choices.why: Correct. Nothing is agreed or argued; the request is logged and routed, and John Doe signs only the approved Limited Release.

choices.label: Tell her the catch-all clause would be unenforceable anyway.
choices.why: That is a legal opinion given to the other side. It is not the Case Manager's to give, and it invites her to say signing is harmless.
